entities.summary: Miriam Altman is a South African economist, business person, social activist, and strategist who has made significant contributions to the development of sustainable economic models and social justice initiatives in Africa. Born in 1967 in Johannesburg, South Africa, Altman has held various leadership positions in the business and non-profit sectors, including serving as the CEO of the International Finance Corporation's Africa Regional Office. Her work has focused on promoting economic development and social transformation in Africa, with a particular emphasis on women's empowerment and environmental sustainability. Altman has received numerous awards for her work, including the 2015 African Business Leadership Award, and has been recognized as one of the most influential people in Africa by Time magazine in 2018. Through her work, Altman has helped to shape the conversation around sustainable economic development and social justice in Africa, and has inspired a new generation of leaders to take up the challenge of creating a more equitable and sustainable future for all. As a result, her legacy will continue to be felt for years to come, and her work will serve as a model for future generations of leaders and activists who seek to create positive change in the world. Altman's commitment to social justice and environmental sustainability has earned her a reputation as a trailblazer in the field of economic development, and her work will be remembered as a key moment in the history of African economic development.
